agent.name: Embedded Project Idea Scoping Agent
agent.context: Embedded Engineering and Gen AI Summer School for third-year Computer Science students
agent.purpose: Convert a vague embedded project idea into a structured scoping brief for requirements engineering

source_input.original_project_idea: A dual-mode embedded audio workstation built on the NXP FRDM-MCXA153 platform, featuring a 2.4-inch ILI9341 SPI TFT LCD with integrated resistive Touchscreen and SD Card storage. The system operates in two main firmware modes selected via an intuitive graphical Touch UI or a wireless web interface: Spectrum Analyzer & Recorder Mode, and Touch Synthesizer & Effects Mode.

fixed_platform.logic_level_policy: Assume 3.3 V logic unless verified otherwise

project.name: Dual-Mode Touchscreen Audio Workstation: Real-Time FFT Analyzer, Smart Recorder & Touch Synthesizer
project.short_summary: A dual-mode embedded audio workstation built on the NXP FRDM-MCXA153 platform, featuring a 2.4-inch ILI9341 SPI TFT LCD with integrated resistive Touchscreen and SD Card storage. Renders 60 FPS FFT spectrum, records WAV to SD Card bare-metal, synthesizes piano notes on Touch UI, outputs via internal DAC to 3.5mm jack, and controls remotely via ESP8266 Wi-Fi web server.
project.main_objective: Build a dual-mode digital audio workstation combining real-time signal analysis (FFT) and recording, bare-metal interactive synthesis, and wireless local web control on a single FRDM-MCXA153 platform.
project.main_behavior: Sampling audio via ADC+DMA, rendering 60 FPS FFT spectrum & oscilloscope on 2.4" TFT LCD, managing bare-metal WAV recording to SD Card, generating synth waveforms with filters, outputting via internal DAC to 3.5mm jack, and serving local web interface via ESP8266.
outputs: MCU integrated DAC output (P3_12) to 3.5mm headphone jack via 1k resistor
interaction_flow: Display Main Menu on Touchscreen (Mode A: Spectrum Analyzer & Recorder vs Mode B: Touch Synthesizer & Effects)
In Mode A: sample mic audio via ADC triggered by CTIMER & DMA, compute FFT (CMSIS-DSP), render 60 FPS spectrum & oscilloscope, record WAV to SD Card

In Mode B: render piano keyboard & XY modulation pad on touchscreen, synthesize waveforms with real-time filters (reverb, low-pass) applied directly to mic input, output via internal DAC to 3.5mm jack
ESP8266 operates as local web server, providing telemetry and remote system control in background via browser
out_of_scope: Direct 5V logic driving without level translation

problem_space.purpose: Demonstrate high-performance real-time DSP, bare-metal DAC audio output, GUI rendering, SPI file system management, and wireless IoT control on Cortex-M33.
problem_space.physical_process_monitored_or_controlled: Acoustic audio signals (20Hz-20kHz) and user touch gestures.
success_criteria: Stable 60 FPS FFT spectrum display on ILI9341 TFT LCD
Reliable WAV audio recording directly to SD Card via FatFS over SPI
Low-latency touch response for synthesizer keyboard and XY pad
Wireless telemetry and control via local ESP8266 Web Server
Clean audio output from DAC to 3.5mm headphone jack
known_constraints: Maximum internal ADC sampling rate 40-50 kHz for audio
SPI bus shared between ILI9341 TFT, resistive Touch, and SD Card slot
unknown_constraints: SPI bus bandwidth limit when driving 320x240 TFT LCD and writing SD Card concurrently
Exact power consumption of ESP8266 web server under standard USB power

core_student_version.description: Basic audio spectrum analyzer rendering live FFT on 2.4" TFT LCD and rendering oscilloscope waveform.
expected_features: ADC audio sampling at 40 kHz via LPADC
Spectrum bar graph and oscilloscope on ILI9341 TFT LCD
core_student_version.why_it_is_suitable: Focuses on core DSP, ADC, DMA, and SPI display drivers without complex file systems or wireless networking.

recommended_summer_school_version.description: Dual-mode Touch Audio Workstation featuring FFT spectrum & oscilloscope recorder, touchscreen piano synth with filters, and internal DAC output.
expected_features: Dual-mode Touch UI (Mode A: Spectrum/Recorder, Mode B: Touch Synth & XY Pad)
Bare-metal WAV file recording to SD Card over FatFS/SPI
Audio synthesis and real-time low-pass/reverb filtering outputted via internal DAC
recommended_summer_school_version.why_it_is_interesting: Combines real-time DSP, touch UI, embedded file systems, and internal DAC audio processing into a rich student demo.
recommended_summer_school_version.why_it_is_still_feasible: Achievable within summer school timeframe using modular drivers and FreeRTOS / superloop architecture.

advanced_extension.description: Full IoT Connected Workstation with local ESP8266 Web Server, remote dashboard telemetry, and remote synth control.
advanced_features: ESP8266 UART Wi-Fi hosting local Web Server
Interactive wireless browser dashboard for remote telemetry
Wireless system control (parameters and mode switching) via browser
technical_challenges: Multi-protocol concurrent communication (SPI TFT, SPI SD, SPI Touch, UART ESP8266)
Interrupt latency and DMA buffer synchronization under web traffic
risk_controls: Isolate ESP8266 communication to non-blocking background UART queues
Provide fallback standalone mode if Wi-Fi connection fails

main_board.name: NXP FRDM-MCXA153
main_board.reasoning: Mandatory board for all summer school projects

sensors.name: MAX4466 Microphone Module
sensors.voltage_or_signal_notes: 3.3V VCC, analog output centered at VCC/2 (1.65V)
risks: Overvoltage input spike if exposed to high volume (requires protection)

actuators_outputs.name: 3.5mm Audio Jack (Output)
actuators_outputs.voltage_or_power_notes: Requires 1k resistor in series with Tip/Ring for protection
risks: Low impedance load direct connection (mitigated by 1k series resistor)

user_inputs.name: Resistive Touchscreen on 2.4" TFT
user_inputs.purpose: GUI menu navigation, piano keyboard, and XY modulation pad
user_inputs.likely_interface: SPI / GPIO (CS on P3_1, IRQ on P2_4)
user_inputs.notes: Requires SPI bus sharing and touch calibration routine

user_inputs.name: Tactile Buttons
user_inputs.purpose: Mode Change (Button 1 on P2_2) and System Reset (Button 2 on RESET)
user_inputs.notes: Directly connected to MCU GPIO pins with internal Pull-up

display_ui.name: 2.4" ILI9341 SPI TFT LCD Display
display_ui.purpose: Real-time FFT spectrum, waveform, and Touch GUI rendering
display_ui.likely_interface: SPI + CS/DC/RST GPIOs (SCK: P2_12, MOSI: P2_13, MISO: P2_16, CS: P2_6, D/C: P3_0, RST: P2_5)

communication_debug.name: ESP8266 Wi-Fi Module
communication_debug.purpose: Local Web Server for wireless telemetry and remote control
communication_debug.likely_interface: UART (115200 baud on LPUART2, TXD to P1_4, RXD to P1_5)
communication_debug.notes: Powered from 3.3V rail; EN/CH_PD must be tied to 3.3V

power_source.recommended_power: Standard USB power supplying the FRDM-MCXA153 board
power_source.notes: 3.3V regulator from board powers display, mic, and ESP8266
risks: High current draw from ESP8266 causing MCU voltage drops (mitigated by decoupling)

software_context.recommended_development_environment: MCUXpresso SDK + CMake + VS Code / MCUXpresso IDE
software_context.suggested_starting_point: FRDM-MCXA153 SDK LPSPI / LPADC / CTIMER / DAC baseline examples

constraints.voltage: Assume 3.3 V logic unless verified otherwise
constraints.timing: FFT calculation & screen refresh loop within 16.6ms (60 FPS)
constraints.safety: Decoupling capacitor (100nF) on mic; 1k protection resistor on DAC output
constraints.privacy_security: Local audio storage on SD Card; wireless telemetry local-only web server

complexity.reason: Uses standard MCUXpresso SDK drivers, CMSIS-DSP library, FatFS over SPI, and modular UART peripheral interfaces.

facts_provided_by_user: Display is 2.4" ILI9341 SPI TFT LCD with integrated resistive Touchscreen and SD Card slot
Audio input via MAX4466 mic on P1_10 (ADC0)
Audio output via internal DAC on P3_12 to 3.5mm jack
Wi-Fi via ESP8266 module on LPUART2 (TXD to P1_4, RXD to P1_5)

assumptions.assumption: The ILI9341 TFT display controller, resistive Touch, and SD Card slot share the SPI0 bus using separate Chip Select (CS) GPIO lines.
assumptions.reason: Standard SPI bus sharing setup for breakout boards

assumptions.assumption: DAC output uses a 1k resistor in series with Tip/Ring to protect the MCU from headphone load impedance.
assumptions.reason: Protects MCXA153 DAC pin from excessive current

open_questions.question: Will SPI bus sharing between LCD, Touch, and SD Card cause audio processing glitches or frame drops?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines if FreeRTOS task prioritization or DMA-backed SPI is required

technical: SPI bus contention between TFT display, Touch, and SD Card
ADC sampling noise from ESP8266 Wi-Fi module power rails
safety: Shorting output if headphones are plugged directly without the 1k series resistor
voltage_power: USB power rail noise causing noise in ADC microphone readings
timing: FFT computation and DAC output generation taking longer than the audio sampling frame time
memory: Audio recording buffer overflowing internal SRAM during SD Card writes
advanced_feature_risks: ESP8266 Web Server dropping incoming connections under heavy DSP loading

human_approval_required: Confirm SPI CS pin allocations for ILI9341, Touch, and SD Card slot

handoff_to_requirements_agent.readiness_notes: Scoping brief is complete and ready for requirements expansion.
